extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2022 reviewers (assigned paper reviewers / program committee reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for reviewers evaluating submissions to ICLR 2022, covering tasks from bidding through discussion and final recommendation, plus ethical and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must meet deadlines for initial review, discussion participation, and final recommendation. Reviews should be detailed enough to support program committee decisions and help authors improve their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: You must adhere to our Code of Ethics in your role as a reviewer. You must also adhere to our Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag any potential CoE violations using the CoE report. For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, paper length/formatting), contact the AC or PC via official OpenReview comment; AC will work with PC and ethics board to resolve CoE issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete main reviewer tasks (workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main reviewer tasks include creating an OpenReview profile and linking DBLP, bidding on papers, writing a constructive/thorough/timely review, discussing with authors/reviewers/ACs, providing a final recommendation, and flagging CoE violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow listed dates for each task (profile by Sept 15; bidding window; review window; discussion phase; final recommendation deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough reading of paper and related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the paper: carefully read through the entire paper, and look up any related work and citations that will help you comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. While reading, note objective of work, strong/weak points, and be mindful of biases. Consult supplementary material if needed (not required but can answer questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess objective(s) of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the objective of the work: Is it to better address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new application/problem, or introduce/explain a new theoretical finding? Or a combination?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations regarding value and impact. Use the objective to frame evaluation of methods and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate strengths (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong points: is the submission clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, does it present novel findings (e.g., theoretically, algorithmically, etc.)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete evidence for strengths (e.g., experiments, proofs, reproducibility artifacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify weaknesses (specific to evaluated aspects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weak points: is it weak in any of the aspects listed in strengths (clarity, correctness, rigor, reproducibility, novelty)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be comprehensive and specific about weaknesses; indicate severity and whether they are addressable during rebuttal/revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rejecting for 'not interesting' alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t reject a paper just because you don’t find it “interesting”. This should not be a criterion at all for accepting/rejecting a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the submission brings sufficient value to parts of the ICLR community even if it's not interesting to you personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three key questions for accept/reject recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer three key questions: (1) What is the specific question/problem tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support the claims (are results correct and scientifically rigorous)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use answers to these to make an explicit accept/reject recommendation and articulate the primary reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the initial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the initial review organized as: summarize the paper's claimed contributions; list strong and weak points; clearly state recommendation (accept or reject) with one or two key reasons; provide supporting arguments; ask questions for authors; provide additional feedback aimed at improving the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be positive and generous in the summary. Make sections easy to navigate for ACs and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite, precise, concrete, and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: General points: Be polite in your review. Be precise and concrete. Provide constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references to back up claims (especially about novelty/prior work). Explicitly state uncertainties. Phrase suggestions to help the authors rather than only criticize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite contemporaneous work and exercise judgement on arXiv vs peer-reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Are authors expected to cite very recent work? We consider papers contemporaneous if published within the last four months; authors may be excused for not knowing papers only on arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to use their own good judgment and discuss with AC if in doubt about omissions in citations/comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary to read supplementary material but such material can often answer questions that arise while reading the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider looking at supplementary material before asking authors questions that could be resolved there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on requesting additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can ask for additional experiments, but make sure you justify why they’re necessary to push the paper over the acceptance threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should not significantly change the content of the submission; they should be limited in scope and serve to more thoroughly validate existing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State on state-of-the-art (SOTA) results
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not achieve state-of-the-art results, that is not by itself grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions bring value when they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, impactful, or insightful knowledge even without SOTA performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: How to avoid/handle assignment conflicts: update your OpenReview profile (co-authors, past/current institutions). If you find a conflicted paper while bidding, bid 'Very Low'. If assigned a conflicted paper, contact program chairs immediately to reassign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict detection relies on profile data; proactively update profile to prevent conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contact the Area Chair (AC)
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact the AC for a paper: go to the OpenReview page for that paper (logged in), add an official comment, fill out the form, and add the ACs to the list of Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use official OpenReview comment mechanism for AC/PC communication and for reporting non-CoE policy violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging and reporting Code of Ethics violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the CoE report: check your assigned papers for conflicts with the Code of Ethics and mark them in your review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about a CoE issue, reach out to your area chair. The AC will coordinate with PC and ethics board if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in discussion phase and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in discussion: reviewers, authors and area chairs engage asynchronously and authors may revise their submissions. It is crucial to be actively engaged and responsive during this phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be able to respond to comments/requests within 3 business days. Update your review in light of discussion and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an updated final recommendation and be open to change
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide final recommendation: update your review taking into account information collected during discussion and any revisions; maintain openness to changing your initial recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final recommendation should reflect rebuttal answers, discussion, and any new evidence; can move more positive or negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review examples and good-review structure (model examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example reviews demonstrate good structure: clear summary, reasons for score, detailed pros and cons, specific requests (e.g., ablation studies), minor comments/typos, and post-rebuttal update explaining stance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use example reviews as templates for thoroughness and tone. Examples illustrate how to present major concerns, suggested experiments, theoretical analysis requests, and minor corrections.
